title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets observed skewed burst consumption on priority buckets where short-lived high-QPS tenants exhausted burst credits without clear visibility. This PR adds priority-aware burst utilization reporting and a small smoothing heuristic to the token-bucket accounting to make autoscaler decisioning and billing dashboards more interpretable.

What changed (single-line description): Added priority-bucket telemetry, improved token-bucket smoothing, exposed new per-priority throughput guarantees, and updated dashboards/alerts.

Details: Implemented a priority-aware aggregator that emits the following new metrics: `dedicated.autoscaler.priority_burst_utilization{priority}`, `dedicated.autoscaler.priority_tokenbucket_smoothing{priority}`, and `dedicated.autoscaler.priority_throughput_guarantee{priority}`. These metrics are emitted at 10s resolution and include p50/p90/p99 windows. The autoscaler logic now consumes the smoothed token-bucket estimate when evaluating burst eligibility to reduce oscillation seen during short bursts.

Compatibility and rollout: Backwards-compatible: default smoothing is disabled unless `autoscaler.priority_smoothing.enabled=true` is set in the fleet config. We will enable the flag for a subset of low-risk fleets (canary group) and monitor `dedicated.autoscaler.priority_burst_utilization` for regressions.

Checklist:
- [x] Core metrics emitted from autoscaler controller
- [x] Unit tests for priority accounting and smoothing logic
- [x] Integration test simulating multi-tenant burst scenarios
- [x] Dashboard updates (Grafana JSON) and alert thresholds added
- [x] Docs snippet in redwood-docs explaining priority burst metrics and flag

Testing notes: Unit and integration tests included. Load testing ran on a 10-fleet synthetic workload demonstrating a 25% reduction in autoscaler thrash across priority buckets and reduced false-positive burst throttles. CI: all checks passed after one lint fix.

Rollout plan: Feature gate off by default. Enable for canary fleets on 2026-02-27, observe 48h, then escalate to broader fleets if metrics are stable. If regressions appear, the autoscaler will fallback to legacy behavior via the `autoscaler.fallback.legacy=true` flag.

References: ENG-1223 (priority autoscaler follow-up), ENG-1308 (observability gap for burst metrics).

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can you confirm the cardinality impact of emitting priority labels on metrics? We have ~50 priority classes in some enterprise fleets.
Maya Chen: Response: We bucket priority into 6 runtime categories (P0..P5) at ingestion to bound cardinality; documented in README and enforced in metric emitter. Added unit tests for mapping.
Lena Hirsch: The smoothing time constant parameters look aggressive; can we make them configurable and set conservative defaults?
Maya Chen: Updated configs/defaults.yaml with `autoscaler.priority_smoothing.window_seconds` and `decay_alpha`. Kept default off and conservative values when enabled.
Noah Kim: Integration test looks good. One nit: the alert threshold for p99 might be too tight for noisy workloads.
Maya Chen: Relaxed alert from 95th to 99th percentile slack in alerts.yaml and added a runbook note.
release_notes: Enhancement: Adds priority-aware burst utilization metrics and optional smoothing to autoscaler token-bucket accounting to reduce thrash and improve observability. Backwards-compatible behind a feature flag.
